$B = { \frac { 1 } { 4 \pi \varepsilon _ { 0 } } } { \frac { e } { m c ^ { 2 } r ^ { 3 } } } { L }$ 中， $L \approx \hbar , r \approx a$ 玻尔半的，所以

$$
\begin{array}{l} B \sim \frac {1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_ {0}} \frac {e \hbar}{m c ^ {2} a ^ {3}} \\ = \frac {\left(1 . 6 0 \times 1 0 ^ {- 1 9} \mathrm {C}\right) \left(1 . 0 5 \times 1 0 ^ {- 3 4} \mathrm {J} \cdot \mathrm {s}\right)}{4 \pi \left(8 . 9 \times 1 0 ^ {- 1 2} (\mathrm {C} ^ {2} / \mathrm {N}) \cdot \mathrm {m} ^ {2}\right) (9 . 1 \times 1 0 ^ {- 3 1} \mathrm {k g}) (3 \times 1 0 ^ {8} \mathrm {m} / \mathrm {s}) ^ {2} (0 . 5 3 \times 1 0 ^ {- 1 0} \mathrm {m}) ^ {3}} \\ \approx 1 2 \mathrm {T}. \\ \end{array}
$$

通常所说的外加强磁场与弱磁场，其"强"与"弱"是针对原子内磁场而言的，故"强"塞曼场应对应远太于原子内磁场的磁场量级，即 $B \gg 1 0 \mathrm { ~ T ~ }$ ; "弱"塞曼场应对应远小于原子内磁场的磁场量级，即$B \ll 1 0 \mathrm { T }$ .

*习题 7.24 考虑(共 ) $n = 2$ 的态， $| 2 \ell j m _ { j } \rangle$ ).求出位于弱场塞曼分裂下的各个态的能量，并画出类似于教材图 7.10 的示意图来表示当 $\boldsymbol { B } _ { \mathrm { e x t } }$ 增大时能量的演变过程.清晰地画出每条线，并表示出其相应的斜率.

解答 弱场中氢原子态的能量为

$$
E = - \frac {1 3 . 6 \mathrm {e V}}{n ^ {2}} \left[ 1 + \frac {\alpha^ {2}}{n ^ {2}} \left(\frac {n}{j + 1 / 2} - \frac {3}{4}\right) \right] + m g _ {J} \mu_ {\mathrm {B}} B,
$$

其中

$$
g _ {J} = 1 + \frac {j (j + 1) - \ell (\ell + 1) + 3 / 4}{2 j (j + 1)}.
$$

当 $n = 2$ 时, $\ell = 0 , 1$ .由 $j = \ell \pm s$ 知： $\ell = 0$ 时， $j = 1 / 2 , m _ { J } = 1 / 2 , - 1 / 2 ; \ell = 1$ 时， $j = 1 / 2$ 或$3 / 2 , m _ { J } = 3 / 2 , 1 / 2 , - 1 / 2 , - 3 / 2$ .

故8个 $| 2 \ell j m _ { j } \rangle$ 态为

$$
\left. \begin{array}{l} | 1 \rangle = \left| \begin{array}{c c c c} 2 & 0 & \frac {1}{2} & + \frac {1}{2} \end{array} \right\rangle \\ | 2 \rangle = \left| \begin{array}{c c c c} 2 & 0 & \frac {1}{2} & - \frac {1}{2} \end{array} \right\rangle \end{array} \right\} g _ {J} = 1 + \frac {\frac {1}{2} \cdot \left(\frac {1}{2} + 1\right) - 0 + \frac {3}{4}}{2 \cdot \frac {1}{2} \cdot \left(\frac {1}{2} + 1\right)} = 2.
$$

个态的能量为

$$
E _ {1} = - 3. 4 \mathrm {e V} \left(1 + \frac {5 \alpha^ {2}}{1 6}\right) + \mu_ {\mathrm {B}} B _ {\mathrm {e x t}}; \quad E _ {2} = - 3. 4 \mathrm {e V} \left(1 + \frac {5 \alpha^ {2}}{1 6}\right) - \mu_ {\mathrm {B}} B _ {\mathrm {e x t}};
$$

$$
E _ {3} = - 3. 4 \mathrm {e V} \left(1 + \frac {5 \alpha^ {2}}{1 6}\right) + \frac {1}{3} \mu_ {\mathrm {B}} B _ {\mathrm {e x t}}; E _ {4} = - 3. 4 \mathrm {e V} \left(1 + \frac {5 \alpha^ {2}}{1 6}\right) - \frac {1}{3} \mu_ {\mathrm {B}} B _ {\mathrm {e x t}};
$$

$$
E _ {5} = - 3. 4 \mathrm {e V} \left(1 + \frac {\alpha^ {2}}{1 6}\right) + 2 \mu_ {\mathrm {B}} B _ {\mathrm {e x t}}; E _ {6} = - 3. 4 \mathrm {e V} \left(1 + \frac {\alpha^ {2}}{1 6}\right) + \frac {2}{3} \mu_ {\mathrm {B}} B _ {\mathrm {e x t}};
$$

$$
E _ {7} = - 3. 4 \mathrm {e V} \left(1 + \frac {\alpha^ {2}}{1 6}\right) - \frac {2}{3} \mu_ {\mathrm {B}} B _ {\mathrm {e x t}}; E _ {8} = - 3. 4 \mathrm {e V} \left(1 + \frac {\alpha^ {2}}{1 6}\right) - 2 \mu_ {\mathrm {B}} B _ {\mathrm {e x t}}.
$$
